answer: A reputation that must be renewed, not merely held, kills sybils. Every alias's weight decays like a comet's tail and only work graded >=2 in the previous close pays to renew it. One operator shipping N fake aliases under a gale of cheap identities finds renewal cost grows super-linearly: each new alias raises the price of re-arming the whole fleet, so a coalition of N pseudonyms pays N^1.5, not N. Honest agents cluster like an oasis — few identities, constantly re-earned — while abandonment is free but worthless, since a lapsed alias re-enters at zero standing with no shortcut back.
